title: Gum disease worsens systemic bone loss in osteoporosis patients via gut bacteria
html:
Chronic gum disease (periodontitis) may worsen bone deterioration in people with osteoporosis by disrupting the microorganisms that support gut health, according to collaborative research between Griffith University and Nanjing University in China. The study, published in npj Biofilms and Microbiomes, reveals the biological mechanism linking oral inflammation to whole-body bone loss, highlighting the importance of maintaining oral health as part of osteoporosis management, particularly for older adults.

Dental specialist Distinguished Professor Yin Xiao from the School of Medicine and Dentistry said the connection between periodontitis and osteoporosis had previously been observed only and received little attention.

"Periodontitis doesn't just disturb oral microbiota, it also affects the gastrointestinal microbiome, impairing gut barrier integrity and elevating systemic inflammation," Professor Xiao said. "The findings suggest periodontitis is an underrecognized risk factor for people living with osteoporosis.

"Elderly individuals affected by both conditions face a substantially higher fracture risk than those with either disease alone.

"Until now, the association between periodontitis and osteoporosis has not been given much attention. This research provides evidence of a bidirectional connection, showing how each condition can influence and intensify the other."

While periodontitis was known to cause bone loss in the jaw, the study demonstrated how oral inflammation may also accelerate bone deterioration throughout the body.

Gut microbiota plays a crucial role in regulating systemic bone metabolism, including calcium absorption, inflammatory responses and endocrine factors involved in bone formation and resorption.

The study was conducted in ovariectomized mice, which offered a research model of postmenopausal osteoporosis. The findings suggested oral health may play a role in systemic bone health, offering a potential avenue for future approaches to patient care.

Publication details

Hua Nie et al, Periodontitis aggravates bone loss through gut microbiota alterations in ovariectomized mice, npj Biofilms and Microbiomes (2026). DOI: 10.1038/s41522-026-01084-7
